title: Jay-Z Closes His Tour With Surprise Guests in Los Angeles
summary: Jay-Z closed his tour with a night full of surprises. At his second concert at Los Angeles' SoFi Stadium, the final gig of the Jay-Z 30 Tour, he brought out Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre, and Too Short. Too Short was the first guest to take the stage, performing his 2006 hit Blow the Whistle, with Jay-Z adding his Playoff freestyle to the track. Later in the show, Jay-Z performed his own song D'Evils over the beat of a Snoop Dogg song, and at that point Snoop Dogg came out onstage. Dr. Dre was next, and Jay-Z handed the stage to the duo, who performed a medley of The Next Episode, California Love, Nothin' But a 'G' Thang, and Still D.R.E. It was a celebration of decades of hip-hop history, all in one set. Before the gig, there were unconfirmed reports on social media that ticket prices for Saturday's show had fallen, with tickets even being given away for free. During Encore, Jay-Z addressed the rumours, and artificial intelligence in general. He told the crowd to be really real about what is going on in the world, and to trust what they could see and hear for themselves. He said people might tell them nobody was there, or that the music was not great, but they had eyes and ears of their own. His message was simple: question everything you feel, especially in a world where technology can trick people. The previous night at SoFi, Jay-Z had brought out his own daughter Blue Ivy for The Story of O.J. and Dead Presidents, Geto Boys' Scarface for This Can't Be Life and Mind Playing Tricks, and DJ Khaled and John Legend for a show-ending God Did. The retrospective Jay-Z 30 Tour opened in July with three star-studded nights at New York's Yankee Stadium, followed by gigs in London and Paris. The Los Angeles finale brought that journey to a close with friends, old songs, and a packed stadium singing along.
why_it_matters: It celebrates decades of hip-hop history shared live with a packed stadium, and it raises a wider point about checking what we see and hear when technology can trick people.

background_read: A concert tour is a series of live shows by a musician in different cities, and a finale is the last show of that run.
Hip-hop is a style of music built around rapping, beats, and DJing, with a long history of artists working together on stage.
Surprise guests are performers who appear without being announced in advance, which can make a final night feel special for the crowd.
Jay-Z's Los Angeles show closed a tour that had opened in New York and then visited London and Paris before reaching its final stadium night.
